stem: A company runs data-processing workers on Amazon EC2 instances in private subnets of a VPC. Each night the workers upload several terabytes of result files to an Amazon S3 bucket in the same AWS Region. All outbound traffic from the private subnets goes through a NAT gateway, and the monthly bill shows high NAT gateway data processing charges. The workers must still download software updates from the internet. The uploads must reach Amazon S3 privately. Which solution will meet these requirements in the MOST cost-effective way?
keywords: upload several terabytes of result files to an Amazon S3 bucket in the same AWS Region
must still download software updates from the internet

options.text: Create an interface endpoint for Amazon S3 in each private subnet, and send the uploads to the DNS name of the interface endpoint.
options.why: It works and stays private, but an interface endpoint is [billed for each hour that your interface VPC endpoint is provisioned in each Availability Zone](../facts/vpc.md#vpc-interface-endpoint-billed-hour-per-az-and-gb) and per GB processed.
options.misconception: every VPC endpoint is free, like a gateway endpoint

options.text: Move the workers to public subnets, assign a public IPv4 address to each worker, and send all traffic through the internet gateway.
options.why: The uploads would leave the private subnets, which breaks the private requirement, and [AWS charges for all public IPv4 addresses](../facts/vpc.md#vpc-public-ipv4-charge-2024).

options.text: Create a gateway endpoint for Amazon S3, and associate the endpoint with the route tables of the private subnets that the workers use.
options.why: Instances in subnets with the endpoint route [automatically use the gateway endpoint to access the service](../facts/vpc.md#vpc-gateway-endpoint-applies-per-route-table), so the uploads stop passing through the NAT gateway.

options.text: Create a NAT gateway in each Availability Zone, and point the route table of each private subnet to the NAT gateway in its zone.
options.why: Each NAT gateway still charges for [each gigabyte of data that it processes](../facts/vpc.md#vpc-natgw-pricing-dimensions), so the upload bytes are still billed for processing.

explanation: The expensive bytes are the uploads to Amazon S3. [Gateway VPC endpoints provide reliable connectivity to Amazon S3 and DynamoDB without requiring an internet gateway or a NAT device for your VPC](../facts/vpc.md#vpc-gateway-endpoint-s3-dynamodb-no-privatelink), and [There are no data processing or hourly charges for using Gateway Type VPC endpoints](../facts/vpc.md#vpc-gateway-endpoint-no-hourly-or-processing-charge). The default route to the NAT gateway stays, so the software updates still work.
takeaway: Send same-Region Amazon S3 traffic through a gateway endpoint, not through a NAT gateway.
twin: If the stem said "servers in the data center upload the files" instead: an interface endpoint, because S3 [gateway endpoints do not allow access from on-premises networks, from peered VPCs in other AWS Regions, or through a transit gateway](../facts/vpc.md#vpc-gateway-endpoint-no-onprem-cross-region-tgw).
say: For S3 in the same Region I'd add a gateway endpoint: no hourly charge and no NAT processing.

stem: A company runs 400 Amazon EC2 instances in public subnets. Each instance has a public IPv4 address so that it can download small operating system updates from the internet each night. Nothing on the internet starts connections to the instances. A cost review shows a large monthly charge for public IPv4 addresses. The instances must keep downloading the updates. Which solution will meet these requirements in the MOST cost-effective way?
keywords: Nothing on the internet starts connections to the instances
large monthly charge for public IPv4 addresses

options.text: Replace the public IPv4 address of each instance with an Elastic IP address, so that the address stays the same and is not billed while in use.
options.why: An Elastic IP address is a public IPv4 address too, and [AWS charges for all public IPv4 addresses](../facts/vpc.md#vpc-public-ipv4-charge-2024), in use or idle.

options.text: Remove the public IPv4 addresses, and place an internet-facing Application Load Balancer in front of the instances for their update traffic.
options.why: A load balancer serves traffic that comes in; the instances start outbound connections, and without public addresses they have no egress path.
options.misconception: a load balancer gives its targets outbound internet access

options.text: Move the instances to private subnets without public IPv4 addresses, and send their outbound traffic through NAT gateways in public subnets.
options.why: A few NAT gateways replace hundreds of billed addresses, and AWS points to this pattern: [use Elastic Load Balancers and NAT Gateways for ingress and egress traffic](../facts/vpc.md#vpc-public-ipv4-avoid-per-instance-with-elb-nat).

options.text: Move the instances to private subnets with NAT gateways, and convert each public IPv4 address to an Elastic IP address that stays allocated for a rollback.
options.why: The updates still work, but [The price is the same whether the public IPv4 address is in-use](../facts/vpc.md#vpc-public-ipv4-hourly-in-use-or-idle) or idle, so the kept addresses still cost money.
options.misconception: an Elastic IP address that is not attached to an instance is free

explanation: Every public IPv4 address is billed: [You pay an hourly rate for each public IPv4 address used by your AWS account](../facts/vpc.md#vpc-public-ipv4-hourly-in-use-or-idle). The instances start all their connections themselves, so they need egress, not public addresses. AWS points to this design to lower the charge: [use Elastic Load Balancers and NAT Gateways for ingress and egress traffic](../facts/vpc.md#vpc-public-ipv4-avoid-per-instance-with-elb-nat).
takeaway: Instances that start every connection themselves belong in private subnets behind a NAT gateway, without public IPv4 addresses.
twin: If the stem said "users on the internet call a web application on the instances" instead: an internet-facing load balancer in front of private instances, because AWS suggests [use Elastic Load Balancers and NAT Gateways for ingress and egress traffic](../facts/vpc.md#vpc-public-ipv4-avoid-per-instance-with-elb-nat).
say: Every public IPv4 address costs money, so I'd move outbound-only instances behind a NAT gateway.
